result.notes:
**What the proposal gets right, and it is most of it.** Every grid value, every calendar line number, every routine string and the intersection arithmetic check out against the raw artifacts — I re-extracted the 2013-08-20 and 2018-07-11 HTML tables, the two 2017 hours JSONs, all three calendar layout files and the four content-api states rather than trusting the synthesis. The 2024-11-04 row is a clean, unconditional, day-level SGX primary and is the single biggest gain in the run: it dates a transition `history.rs` currently calls undated, dissolves an intersection that was costing thirty minutes of T session and thirty of T+1 open across four years, and — the part worth keeping in the module comment — sources the routines on both sides of itself, which is exactly what the existing note says a circular could not do. The `members`/`non_members` analysis is careful and correct: JP (MSCI Japan) carrying the identical grid in the 2018 edition and still not being a Nikkei contract is precisely the trap LAW-PRIMARY-SOURCES' "a venue that merely coincides with another still gets its own named profile" is written for, and the 2021-edition negative on the Singapore "FTSE successor" premise is a genuinely useful finding for the sibling agents.

**Why I refuted anyway.** The brief says default to refuted when uncertain, and I am not uncertain about two things: the row-kind label on 2017-07-05 is wrong under AGENTS.md's own one-sentence definition of a knowledge boundary, and there is a sourced SGX-versus-SGX contradiction fifty minutes from the corroborating capture that the proposal does not know about. The second is the one I would not ship without. The proposal's whole case for the date is that a contemporaneous contract set proves an undated SGX portal grid current; the commodities page has a contemporaneous contract set and was serving a grid SGX had already replaced. That is not a hypothetical about staleness — it is the same operator, the same portal, the same day, the same contract, two different closes.

**Direction-of-error note, since the crate cares about it more than about row count.** My correction moves ~six months (2017-07-05..2017-12-25) from the wider grid to the narrower one. That under-reports: it never says open when SGX was closed. The proposal's version, if the 21 Sep 2017 newsletter turns out to be the effective date, over-reports 14:25–14:55 and 02:00–04:45 nightly for about three months — a false open in executable hours, the failure `cme_nikkei.rs` was explicitly rewritten to remove ("An earlier revision of this module did exactly that, on the reasoning that no source named a cutover"). Asymmetric risk, and cheap to avoid.

**Things the integrator will have to settle across the five families, which this agent could not.** (i) The routines question in E3 has to be answered once for the whole family, not per row — either the 2013 page's stated 4-minute-plus-1-minute shape composes against a printed close or it does not. (ii) If the other four families key their pre-2020 boundaries to different dates from Japan's, the shared `history.rs` paragraph can no longer speak for all five in one voice; the proposal's open question 7 is right about that and it is a real documentation decision. (iii) LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES applies to every open question in the proposal — the unidentified notice behind the S0→A move, the 2014–2016 wcm sweep, the day of the 04:45→05:15 move, and now the commodities/derivatives portal conflict — each needs a GitHub issue opened and cited before the change merges, not a line in a research note. (iv) `SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_CLOSED` must survive the Japan key's baseline change; it is still the baseline for China and Singapore. (v) Any row added or moved must reach `HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS` in `tests/contract/session_invariants/historical_expectations.rs` by hand — the proposal does not mention it, and the fence is deliberately handwritten.

I edited nothing in the repository.

result.law_violations:
**V1 (decisive) — the 2013-08-20 row uses a Wayback capture as a *cutover*, in the closing direction, against the very artifact it cites. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES.**

Compare the proposal's own two pre-2017 rows, bound by bound:

    floor      T 09:00-15:25   T+1 16:40-02:00
    2013-08-20 T 09:00-15:55   T+1 17:00-02:00

The T close moves outward (15:25 -> 15:55): that is a knowledge boundary — "from here we have a source saying the window is at least this wide." But **the T+1 open moves inward, 16:40 -> 17:00.** That is not a change of knowledge; it is an assertion that a window which was open became closed. It is keyed to 2013-08-20 — and I re-read `WB-20130820090335-portal-trading_hours_calendar.html` this session: its normal-week table, captioned "Trading Hours* for SGX Derivatives Market", reads

    SGX FTSE China A50 Index Futures | 9.00am to 3.55pm | 4.40pm to 2.00am

So on the exact day the row is keyed to, the only surviving SGX artifact says the T+1 session was **open at 16:40**, and the proposal's row says it was closed. Under AGENTS.md step 5 this must be recorded in `HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS` as an observable dated profile change, where the next reader will find "2013-08-20: SGX A50 T+1 open 16:40 -> 17:00" and read it as sourced. It is sourced by nothing. That is exactly what LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES forbids: "a historical cutover exists only when a primary source states an unconditional, day-level effective date. A real change without one is documented as a known gap, never given an invented date."

The proposal's defence — "a capture is a knowledge boundary, never a cutover... nothing is claimed to have changed" — does not survive the direction test. A boundary that only *widens* can honestly be labelled knowledge; a boundary that *narrows* is a claim about the market, whatever the citation string says. The proposal sees the anomaly and waves it through: "the two intervals are not nested... That is the correct shape, not an anomaly." It is the tell.

The crate's own worked example says so. "CME's Sunday Pre-Open ... sourced at 16:15 at the floor and 16:00 currently, so 16:15-17:00 is carried from the floor with no cutover asserted and only the 16:00-16:15 quarter-hour waits on the undated 2012 move." CME does **not** re-grant the quarter-hour before the date the 16:00 source appears and withdraw it after. The disputed remainder is withheld across the *whole* undated span. Here the disputed remainder on the T+1 open (16:40-17:00, disputed between S0 and A on an undated changeover) must likewise be withheld from the floor, not surrendered at a capture.

Note this is the one family where the defect bites. For Japan, Singapore and MSCI Taiwan, W == S0, so the floor split is pure widening at every bound and the anomaly never appears. China is where the orchestrator's template breaks, and the proposal adopted the template rather than testing it.

Fix: set the T+1 open to 17:00 in the floor baseline as well. The 2013-08-20 row then becomes pure widening (T close 15:25 -> 15:55) and is admissible as a knowledge boundary. Cost: 20 minutes of T+1 withheld from the floor era that both W and S0 attest — an under-report, the safe direction, and the price of not asserting an unsourced closure.

**V2 — the 2018-10-30 row leaves a 16-month hole in an *executable* phase that the evidence brackets on both sides. "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor" + "Executable windows are the priority."**

The proposal starts `extended` 16:30-16:35 at 2018-10-30 on the ground that this is "the first source that lists the modelled product WITH its routine times." That ground is false (see E1). SGX's 2013 portal page states, in its own words, that *every* equity-index futures contract carries the closing routine and states its exact duration; the T close is unanimous at 16:30 across A, B, B' and C from 2017-07-05; and 16:30-16:35 is confirmed explicitly at 2018-10-30, 2019-01-16, 2019-02-04, 2019-06-11, 2020-01-09 and again in DT/AM 15 of 2025's Current column. The window therefore holds under every sourced state in [2017-07-05, 2018-10-30) — "serve the window that holds under *every* sourced state and withhold only the disputed remainder." Withholding it instead models the A50's closing auction as non-existent for sixteen months, and the closing routine is where a trade prints: "a gap in a phase where a trade can print — `regular` or `extended` — is materially more serious than a gap in an `order_entry` window."

The `order_entry` half of that row survives: the 2013 note affirms the opening routines exist but gives no clock times, so 08:45-09:00 / 16:50-17:00 genuinely first appear on 2018-10-30.

**Not violations (tested and cleared).** No row extends the family onto a non-member: MSCI China (CH/CHO) is correctly excluded — I confirmed the 2017-09-27 capture prints "CHO | SGX MSCI China Index Options | 9.00 am to 4.35 pm", a different product on a different clock — as are NCH and the ex-China NTR contracts and the "China" commodities. The FTSE Xinhua -> FTSE China rename is a rename of one index behind one contract, not the MSCI-Taiwan-vs-FTSE-Taiwan case. DT/AM 50 of 2024 does enumerate NK, NKO, NR, ND, NU, NS, NC, EJRT, EJP only — verified in the mirror file — so declining to split the 2020 era is right. And no state is carried across a sourced contradiction: every disputed span is intersected, not carried.
result.evidence_errors:
**E1 (substantive) — "no artifact states China routines before 2018-10-30" is false, and it is false inside the document the proposal itself mines.** The floor row's `why` asserts "Routines are empty: no artifact states China routines before 2018-10-30, and the portal grid's own footnote says the times 'exclude the pre-opening, pre-closing and respective non-cancel session states.'" Residual risk 8 repeats it: "The 2017 and 2013 portal grids carry the footnote ... so they are **silent** on routines rather than denying them."

The 2013 page is not silent. `WB-20130820090335-portal-trading_hours_calendar.html` carries a "Notes" block, general in scope and not date-keyed, which I re-read verbatim:

  "All equity index futures and interest rate futures contracts are subject to a pre-opening routine and non-cancel period before the start of the T session and T+1 session."
  "All equity index futures contracts are subject to a 4-minute pre-closing routine before the close of the T session, followed by a 1-minute non-cancel period at the end of the T session."

That is a primary source, in SGX's own voice, stating (a) that both opening routines exist for this family from at least 2013, and (b) the closing routine's exact duration, 4 + 1 = 5 minutes, attaching to the published T close. Applied to the A grid's 16:30 close it yields 16:30-16:35 — precisely what the 2018-10-30 spec page then prints. The proposal read this document closely enough to mine its per-holiday tables for the ordering argument and missed the notes directly beneath them. This is what turns V2 from a preference into a correction.

(The note reads "before the close of the T session ... at the end of the T session", which taken alone could place the 5 minutes *inside* the published close. The same page's grid footnote — timings "exclude the pre-opening, pre-closing and respective non-cancel session states" — settles it the other way, and the 2018 spec page confirms: "Opening: 9.00 am - 4.30 pm | Pre - Closing: 4.30 pm - 4.34 pm | Non - Cancel: 4.34 pm - 4.35 pm". The routine follows the published close.)

**E2 — the 2020-01-01 row gains phases its citation does not state.** The proposal amends the shipped row to carry `extended` 16:30-16:35 and `order_entry` 08:45-09:00 / 16:50-17:00 while keeping the citation string "first sourced SGX calendar edition" explicitly UNCHANGED. result.notes:
**What the proposal got right, and it is most of it.** The family membership work is sound and I could not break it: the FTSE Xinhua -> FTSE China rename is one contract under one code whose index provider rebranded, not the MSCI-Taiwan-vs-FTSE-Taiwan case (different contracts, different codes, own launch release); MSCI China (CH/CHO) is correctly excluded and I confirmed it runs a different clock in the same 2017 table; NCH and the ex-China NTR contracts belong to the NTR key; the "China" commodities are not equity index at all; H50 joins as catalog data without moving the boundary. The intersection arithmetic is correct bound by bound in all three intervals as computed. The staleness-direction argument — a served page can be stale but never early, so a capture is a sound upper bound on onset and can only under-date — is the right argument and I have kept it. The 2013 holiday-table ordering corroboration is real and I verified it independently. Residual risk 7's transcription resolution is correct. The refusal to split at 2024-11-04 is correct.

**Why refuted anyway.** Two things. First, the floor split is the right *idea* — this genuinely is the family where W and S0 disagree and a single carried state would over-report the pre-2013 T session — but the proposal executed it by intersecting each interval independently and shipping whatever fell out, including a bound that moves *inward* at a Wayback timestamp. It saw the non-nesting and explicitly blessed it. Under the crate's own CME worked example, a disputed remainder on an undated changeover is withheld across the whole span, never re-granted before a capture and withdrawn after. Second, the routine reasoning rests on a factual claim about the 2013 page that the page itself contradicts, three lines below the tables the proposal quotes.

**One asymmetry worth keeping in the comment.** W enters only through intersections, and an intersection can only narrow. So if W were misidentified — wrong contract, wrong era, wrong page — the error is one-directional and conservative: the floor row would under-report by thirty minutes of T, never over-report. That is worth saying beside the table, because it is the reason the undated orphan is safe to use at all. No artifact in evidence prints a contract code next to "FTSE Xinhua China A50"; the identity rests on its position in the same portal table plus the public history of the index rename.

**Open points I did not force into the table.**
1. `order_entry` 08:45-09:00 attaches to a 09:00 T open that is unanimous in W, S0, A, B, B' and C. Read literally, "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor" would extend that one window to the floor, and at minimum to 2017-07-05, which would dissolve Row 4 entirely. I left it at 2018-10-30 because the pre-opening's thirteen-minute length is genuinely unsourced before then and the phase is the lower-priority kind — but a reviewer who applies carry-back strictly should collapse Row 4 into Row 3 rather than the reverse.
2. The 2018 (Apr) calendar states in SGX's own words "All dates and information are accurate as of 26 December 2017" and carries CreationDate 2018-04-11 — a *document's own date*, which AGENTS.md ranks above a capture for establishing order. It is a stronger citation than 2017-07-05 but a later one, so keying Row 3 to it would cost five months of A coverage. Row 3 stays on the capture, and the 2017-12-26 as-of line belongs in the comment as independent corroboration that A was in force before the 2018 calendar shipped.
3. Rows 2, 3 and 4 fall on a Tuesday, a Wednesday and a Tuesday. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES' "a day-level revision boundary never splits a running session" is written for sourced cutovers and these rows assert no change, so nothing about a session's behaviour changes mid-flight — only the crate's knowledge does, and the shipped 2020-01-01 row (a Wednesday) already has that shape. The proposal is right that this is family-wide and should be decided once, not per key.
4. The proposal's ledger says "the crate's DIRECTION OF THE ERROR note"; I did not locate such a note in `sgx_equity_index.rs` or `history.rs`. If it is a paraphrase of the module's Partial basis rather than a quoted heading, the wording should be fixed before it lands.
5. Adopting a China-specific baseline changes what pre-2010 instants resolve to for this key, from sessionless to the carried grid. AGENTS.md sanctions it ("the profile returned is the oldest state the crate has sourced for that venue"), but the proposal is right that it is an observable behaviour change and belongs in the changelog — and the change set also has to reach `HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS`, the handwritten key baselines, `docs/schedules/verification.md` and the README, none of which the proposal enumerates.

No repository files were edited.

result.shared_boundaries:
FIVE DATES MUST BE IDENTICAL ACROSS THE FAMILIES THAT SHARE THEIR ARTIFACT, AND ONE RULE DECIDES EACH. Every artifact quoted below I re-read from the bytes this session rather than from a proposal or a synthesis.

(1) THE FLOOR. Law quoted: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor. When a phase is primary-sourced at some instant and no primary source names a cutover between the January-2010 floor and that instant, extend it backwards to the floor rather than modelling the interval as sessionless ... Modelling a venue that was demonstrably trading as closed is a worse error than carrying its earliest sourced grid: absence is a claim too." Its precondition is that the MODELLED FAMILY is sourced at some instant, which the knowledge-boundary bullet defines: "A knowledge boundary is the first source that lists the modelled product ... A document only sources a family if that family appears in it." So the floor splits three-two, and it is not a preference: Japan, China and Singapore have members listed WITH A GRID in the oldest artifacts and are carried to the floor as `select_revision` BASELINES asserting no revision row; FTSE Taiwan and the NTR (USD) suite did not exist and stay sessionless below their own launch/first-listing boundaries. The `effective` dates "2010-01-01" printed on the three carried rows are interval labels only — those rows are the baseline argument, carry no date and no citation slot, and govern below the floor too ("Do not add a lower bound to the timelines"). This corrects the Singapore proposal, which printed its floor row as a dated `intersection-start`; the Singapore skeptic quoted the law and is right.

(2) 2013-08-20 — CHINA ONLY, and the reason is the ordering artifact, not a preference. I extracted the wcm/connect fragment (capture 20180711020353) and the portal Trading Hours table (capture 20130820090335) side by side. For Japan every Nikkei row is identical in both (NK/NU 7.45am–2.25pm / 3.15pm–2.00am, NKO 2.30pm, NS 3.25pm/4.15pm, ND 5.55pm/6.45pm); for Singapore MSCI S'pore is identical in both (8.30am–5.10pm / 6.15pm–2.00am, options 5.15pm). Only A50 differs — W "FTSE Xinhua China A50 | 9.00 am - 3.25 pm | 4.10 pm - 2.00 am" against S0 "SGX FTSE China A50 Index Futures | 9.00am to 3.55pm | 4.40pm to 2.00am". So only China's floor interval holds two states and only China splits. W is placed BEFORE S0 on its content, never its capture: its set still names "S&P CNX Nifty", "FTSE Xinhua China A50", "MSCI Asia Apex 50", "MSCI Hong Kong+", no FX and no iron ore. Corroborated: the SAME 2013-08-20 document's seven per-holiday tables print A50 at "9.00am to 3.25pm | 4.10pm to 2.00am" — W's grid — while its normal-week table prints 3.55pm/4.40pm, and every neighbouring contract in those tables matches its own normal-week row (I verified all twelve A50 cells). That is used for ORDER only; per-date data is caller-owned under LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE. Its weight is limited and the skeptic is right that the contract set carries the ordering on its own: A50 is the only contract that diverges there and three of the seven dates postdate the capture.

(3) 2017-07-10 — THE STATE-A BOUNDARY, SHARED BY JAPAN, CHINA AND SINGAPORE. The evidence date is the portal capture 20170705000242 (= 2017-07-05 08:02 SGT, twenty-eight minutes before that day's open), whose parsed grid is byte-identical to capture 20170927124017 twelve weeks later; I diffed the eleven equity rows and they match to the character. A CAPTURE TIMESTAMP IS USED HERE AS A KNOWLEDGE BOUNDARY AND NEVER AS A CUTOVER: nothing is claimed to have changed that day, and the real S0→A move is undated. I reject the Japan skeptic's move to 2017-12-26 and I reject both skeptics' framing of the risk as staleness, for three reasons drawn from evidence neither had. First, direction: a served page can be STALE, never EARLY, so a capture is a sound upper bound on a state's onset and can only under-date it — proved twice over in this corpus, by W (a c.2012 state served in 2018) and by SGX's own commodities hours page, which on 2017-09-27 at 13:30 UTC still printed Fuel Oil 380cst and TSI Iron Ore at "2.00 am (following day)" fifty minutes after the derivatives page printed 4.45am for the same contracts (I extracted both; the commodities page contains zero equity-index rows, so it is not a source conflict on any modelled family — it is proof that SGX served stale trees concurrently). Second, the only failure that could make the capture wrong is PREMATURE PUBLICATION, and SGX's own Derivatives Products Description change log now closes it: row 26, issued 2016-04-22, "Equity Index & Dividend Index products T/T+1 gap increased to 15mins" — which describes state A's shape exactly, since A leaves fifteen minutes between the end of each family's closing routine and its T+1 pre-open — and row 27, issued 2016-07-15, "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours". State A most likely began in 2016, so 2017-07-05 already under-reports by a year and cannot be early. Third, the change log's own "Change of Trading Hours" entry is issued 2017-10-05, AFTER both captures, which independently retires the "21 Sep 2017 newsletter" objection. THE KEY MOVES FROM 2017-07-05 (Wed) TO MONDAY 2017-07-10 for boundary hygiene — see (5).

(4) 2020-01-01 — KEPT, ON ALL FIVE KEYS, WITH TWO CONSEQUENTIAL EDITS. The date and the T-session bounds stand on the 2020 edition and the content-api capture 20200109051211. Its citation string "first sourced SGX calendar edition" becomes false once earlier rows exist and must be restated. Its ROUTINES are forced in, on all five keys at once: capture 20200109051211 is identical to the 2019-06-11 payload except that every "Opening: ... - 4.45 am" reads "5.15 am", so it states each family's Pre-Opening/Non-Cancel/Pre-Closing windows INSIDE this row's interval. Adding them to the earlier eras and dropping them here would assert that SGX deleted its own auction routines on New Year's Day 2020, which no source says; adding them to one key and not its siblings would have the crate report an 18:30–18:35 closing auction for NTR that it denies to Japan on the identical payload. All five or none — all five. This retires history.rs's sentence "Routines stay out of the first era deliberately: the calendars state session bounds only, and the circular's 'current' column is the state after the undated Japan move, not before it": the calendars are silent but SGX's content-api is not, and DT/AM 50 now sources the Japan routines on both sides of 2024-11-04. Japan alone splits this era at 2024-11-04; DT/AM 50 enumerates NK, NKO, NR, ND, NU, NS, NC, EJRT, EJP "(collectively, 'Contracts')" and no China, Singapore, Taiwan or NTR contract, so the other four run unbroken to 2025-04-06.

(5) BOUNDARY HYGIENE — WHY TWO ROWS ARE KEYED TO THE FOLLOWING MONDAY. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: "Day-level revision rows are keyed to the local opening day of the first session they govern, and a day-level revision boundary never splits a running session." `select_revision` picks the profile from the QUERY instant's local date, so a boundary that LENGTHENS or CREATES a wrapping overnight close reports the previous evening's leg running past the close that was in force when it opened. A Wednesday 2017-07-05 key would report Japan/China/Singapore open from 02:00 to 04:45 on that one morning on a leg that opened Tuesday under the 02:00 regime — a false open, which the module's own "DIRECTION OF THE ERROR" note says these rows can no longer produce. Keying to Monday 2017-07-10 removes it exactly, because the rules are Mon-Fri and no leg wraps into a Monday morning (Friday's leg ends Saturday 05:15). Same for the NTR key's sessionless→grid boundary, moved from Wednesday 2018-04-11 to Monday 2018-04-16. Every other boundary here needs no rounding and keeps its artifact's date: 2013-08-20 (Tue) changes only a daytime close, 2019-02-06 (Wed) narrows a T+1 open, 2019-06-11 (Tue) changes only a daytime close, 2020-07-20 is already a Monday. The shipped 2020-01-01 rows have the lengthening shape but are harmless in practice because 1 January is a closed date and "A closed date normally removes its complete trading day, including the prior-evening wrap"; they are left alone.

(6) THE ONE PENDING DECISION THAT WOULD CHANGE THREE OF THESE ROWS, STATED ONCE. Two proposals assert that no SGX-authored channel states a day for the 2019 T+1 extension ("Every SGX-authored channel that could carry a day is closed") and that 2016 is a hole. Both claims are FALSE and must not ship — this is the exact "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists'" failure the law was written about. SGX's Derivatives Products Description change log, downloaded live from api2.sgx.com and held at raw/catalogue/v17.6/, states day-level effective dates in the same form as the two circulars this crate already trusts. I re-parsed the OOXML independently (zipfile + ElementTree, sheet1.xml, mergeCells = 0) and confirm verbatim: r76, issued 2019-05-21, v6.1, single cell — "Amended trading hours for SGP, SGPO and ST eff 10 Jun"; r87–r89 inside one border-partitioned entry whose dated row r90 is 2019-10-07 v6.9 — "Effective 11 Nov:" / "Editorial change Contracts_mainmenu:" / "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts"; and the calibrators r163, issued 2024-11-04, "Amend trading hours of SGX Nikkei Derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures (eff 4 Nov)" = DT/AM 50, and r170, issued 2025-03-19, "(eff 7 Apr)" = DT/AM 15. Admitting this channel is recorded in the store as DECISION PENDING with the maintainer (2026-09-06-catalogue-changelog-REVERSAL.md, issue #45), and the brief I was given states the 04:45→05:15 move has no day, so I build the conservative table — but the refinement is mechanical, not a re-derivation: accepting the channel replaces Singapore's two rows 2019-02-06 and 2019-06-11 with ONE dated cutover at Monday 2019-06-10 (r76 needs no scoping inference at all and is the strongest of the three), and moves the 05:15 T+1 close on ALL FIVE keys from 2020-01-01 back to Monday 2019-11-11 (r89, which needs the one interpretive step of scoping a header row to the items below it inside a single file-encoded entry). Rows 26 and 27 state no effective day and therefore date nothing either way; they only prove the 2016 negative false.

rows.citation: earliest sourced SGX Nikkei grid, carried to the January-2010 floor
rows.why: ENCODED AS THE KEY'S `select_revision` BASELINE, NOT A `revisions!` ROW — it asserts no effective date and no citation slot, and the 2010-01-01 above is an interval label only. It replaces SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_CLOSED for this key. LAW quoted: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor ... This asserts *no* revision row, so it does not fabricate a date - it declines to invent one, exactly as ICE Sugar's August-2011 baseline is carried back." ARTIFACTS: the portal capture 20130820090335, main table, verbatim "SGX Nikkei 225 Index Futures / SGX USD Nikkei 225 Index Futures | 7.45am to 2.25pm | 3.15pm to 2.00am", plus the wcm fragment whose content dates to c.2012 and whose five Nikkei rows are identical — so W introduces no distinct Japan grid and the ordering problem that troubles China is inert here. This is also the sourced intersection with the next state, since A contains S0 in every bound (07:30<07:45, same 14:25 close, 14:55<15:15, 04:45>02:00), so carry-back and intersection give the same table and no choice has to be defended. EXTENDED IS SOURCED IN-ERA, NOT CARRIED FROM 2019 — this is where I side with both skeptics against the proposal, which withheld it here and served it from 2017 on identical reasoning. The 2013 page's own Notes block, extracted verbatim, states the rule and its durations: "All equity index futures contracts are subject to a 4-minute pre-closing routine before the close of the T session, followed by a 1-minute non-cancel period at the end of the T session", under the grid footnote "All timings exclude pre-opening and pre-closing routines, the respective non-cancel periods as well as the respective order-cancellation session states." That the routine FOLLOWS the printed close rather than sitting inside it is not an inference: the SGX FTSE China A50 contract specification captured the same morning (20130820082329) prints "Opening: 9.00 am - 3.55 pm | Pre - Closing: 3.55 pm - 3.59 pm | Non - Cancel: 3.59 pm - 4.00 pm" against that page's printed 3.55pm grid close. Composed against a T close of 14:25 that is unanimous in W and S0, the rule gives 14:25-14:30, and the content-api later prints exactly "Pre-Closing : 2.25 pm - 2.29 pm / Non-Cancel : 2. 29 pm - 2.30 pm" against the identical 14:25. ORDER_ENTRY WITHHELD: the same Notes block attests the opening routines exist but states no duration, and the A-era windows attach to a 07:30 open and a 14:55 reopen this grid does not have. That is an order_entry gap, the lower-priority kind, and open question 3 names the artifact that would close it.

rows.citation: SGX derivatives Trading Hours page, captures 2017-07-05 and 2017-09-27
rows.why: KIND (c), NOT (a) — I accept the skeptic's label correction. Under the brief's own taxonomy a knowledge boundary is "the first artifact listing the modelled family with a grid", and NK/NU are listed with a grid from 2013, so this family has exactly one knowledge boundary and it is the baseline row above. This row starts the interval whose admissible states are A, B, B' and C, and their intersection is A itself. A CAPTURE TIMESTAMP IS THE EVIDENCE HERE AND IS NEVER A CUTOVER: SGX changed nothing on 2017-07-05 and the real S0→A move is undated, now bracketed on the early side by SGX's own change log (r26 2016-04-22 "Equity Index & Dividend Index products T/T+1 gap increased to 15mins", r27 2016-07-15 "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours"). ARTIFACT: capture 20170705000242, "SGX Nikkei 225 Index Futures | 7.30 am to 2.25 pm | 2.55 pm to 4.45 am", byte-identical at 20170927124017, restated by the 2018 (Apr) calendar (own as-of "26 December 2017") and the 2019 calendar. WHY MONDAY 2017-07-10 AND NOT THE CAPTURE DAY: this row lengthens a wrapping overnight close from 02:00 to 04:45, and `select_revision` keys on the query's local date, so a Wednesday boundary would report the Tuesday-night leg open from 02:00 to 04:45 on that one morning — a false open on a leg that opened under the 02:00 regime. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: "a day-level revision boundary never splits a running session." Monday cures it exactly, because both rules are Mon-Fri and nothing wraps into a Monday morning. Cost: three trading days served on the narrower floor grid, the safe direction. INTERSECTION OVER THE INTERVAL, bound by bound: T open max(07:30,07:30)=07:30; T close min(14:25,14:25)=14:25; T+1 open max(14:55,14:55)=14:55; T+1 close min(04:45,05:15)=04:45 — so the undated 04:45→05:15 move is absorbed conservatively and the served window equals A. ROUTINES: printed verbatim by content-api 20190204200905 ("Pre -Opening : 7.15 am - 7.28 am / Non -Cancel : 7.28 am - 7.30 am", T+1 "Pre -Opening : 2.45 pm - 2.53 pm / Non -Cancel : 2.53 pm - 2.55 pm"), byte-identical at 20190611051800 and 20190621080419 and repeated unchanged in DT/AM 50's Current column in 2024; carried back across an interval in which no sourced bound moves. Each contiguous Pre-Opening + Non-Cancel pair merges to one `order_entry` window because its matching lands on an open that already begins a `regular` window; the closing pair stays `extended` because it matches at a single price.

rows.citation: SGX Derivatives Trading Calendar 2020 edition: T+1 close 05:15

(i) Its role: it is no longer the first sourced edition, so the citation string "first sourced SGX calendar edition" is now false and must be restated. (ii) Its T+1 OPEN WIDENS from the shipped 15:25 to 14:55. The 15:25 existed only to absorb the then-undated 2024 Japan move; DT/AM 50 dates that move, the intersection dissolves, and this row now serves what the 2020, 2021-01, 2021-07, 2022-06 and 2024 editions actually print — 2.55 pm — confirmed by DT/AM 50's own Current column, "Opening: 2.55 pm – 5.15am". So the one circular sources the routines on BOTH sides of its own cutover, which is precisely what history.rs's note said could not be done. UNDER-REPORT ACCEPTED AND NAMED: SGX's own voice puts the 04:45→05:15 move in "November 2019" (Annual Report 2020) with no day, so about seven weeks of late 2019 are served thirty minutes short at the T+1 close — see open question 1 for the pending refinement that would close it at 2019-11-11.

rows.citation: SGX-DT Circular DT/AM 50 of 2024
rows.why: THE ONLY DATED CUTOVER THIS WORKSTREAM ADDS, IN SGX'S OWN WORDS. SGX Circular No. DT/AM – 50 of 2024, 9 September 2024, "Extension of T-session for SGX Japan Derivatives and Intraday Margin Cycle 2 Timing Change", Singapore Exchange Derivatives Trading Limited letterhead, signed Leno Lee, SVP Trading and Clearing Services: "with effect from Monday, 4 November 2024, the T session trading hours for SGX Nikkei derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures will be extended by 30 minutes." Section A lists the nine contracts by code. This satisfies LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES' "unconditional, day-level effective date" — the JPX dependency it cites was itself settled by JPX's release of 2024-11-03 confirming the 5 November go-live. Independently corroborated in a second SGX-authored channel: the Derivatives Products Description change log, r163, issued 2024-11-04, "Amend trading hours of SGX Nikkei Derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures (eff 4 Nov)". WHAT THE REVISED COLUMN SOURCES: `regular` T 7.30 am – 2.55 pm and T+1 3.25 pm – 5.15 am; `extended` from "Pre-Closing: 2.55 pm – 2.59 pm / Non-Cancel: 2.59 pm – 3.00 pm"; `order_entry` from "Pre-Opening: 7.15 am – 7.28 am / Non-Cancel: 7.28 am – 7.30 am" (unchanged) and "Pre-Opening: 3.15 pm – 3.23 pm / Non-Cancel: 3.23 pm – 3.25 pm". BOUNDARY HYGIENE: a Monday; the preceding session is Friday 2024-11-01's T+1 leg ending Saturday 05:15, so nothing is split. The circular's footnote "4 November 2024 is a Japan public holiday and its underlying cash market is closed" does NOT make this a holiday row — it is a sourced, persistent change to the recurring week, and the Japan holiday itself is caller-owned DayPolicy data under LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE. CHANNEL: SGX purged its own copy (api2 probes for 2024-09 through 2024-11 return 404); read from a verbatim Fubon Futures member mirror via Wayback capture 20241114183232, the same source class as the CITIC mirror of DT/AM 15 that sources.md's channel-limit note already prescribes.

rows.citation: SGX-DT Circular DT/AM 15 of 2025
rows.why: UNCHANGED — this is SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_JAPAN_BASELINE exactly as it ships, and nothing in the 2026-09-06 evidence touches it. DT/AM 15 of 2025, 24 February 2025, "with effect from Monday, [7] April 2025", Appendix A's revised Japan column 15:05 / 15:08 / 15:10, Appendix B repeating the unchanged T-session and closing routines. Corroborated by change-log r170, issued 2025-03-19, "(eff 7 Apr)". DT/AM 50 independently confirms the two circulars describe successive states of one grid: its Revised T+1 open 15:25 is exactly DT/AM 15's Current column, and its T bounds 07:30–14:55 with the 14:55–15:00 closing routine are exactly what DT/AM 15 says it leaves alone.

per_family.floor_decision: (i) CARRIED, and for this family the two candidate constructions coincide exactly, so no choice has to be defended. LAW quoted in full: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor. When a phase is primary-sourced at some instant and no primary source names a cutover between the January-2010 floor and that instant, extend it backwards to the floor rather than modelling the interval as sessionless. This asserts *no* revision row, so it does not fabricate a date - it declines to invent one, exactly as ICE Sugar's August-2011 baseline is carried back. Modelling a venue that was demonstrably trading as closed is a worse error than carrying its earliest sourced grid: absence is a claim too." And: "Prefer the sourced intersection to omission ... serve the window that holds under *every* sourced state and withhold only the disputed remainder." INTERSECTION COMPUTED BOUND BY BOUND, S0 ∩ A: T open max(07:45,07:30)=07:45 to min(14:25,14:25)=14:25; T+1 open max(15:15,14:55)=15:15 to min(02:00,04:45)=02:00. That is S0 exactly, because A strictly contains S0 in both phases. So carry-back of the earliest sourced state and the sourced intersection with the next state produce the same table; nothing is withheld and nothing extra is asserted. WHY NOT SESSIONLESS: the existing note's stated reason — "no edition of the calendar survives before it" — is now known false. The 2018 (Apr) and 2019 editions are still served live from api2.sgx.com and SGX's own hours page sits in the archive from 2013. Under "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists' ... A sessionless era is a safe answer either way, but the stated reason has to be true", the blackout must go. W TREATED BY ITS CONTENT DATE, AND WHAT THAT IMPLIES: its contract set places it around 2012, and its five Nikkei rows are identical to S0's, so placing it at its content date merely pushes the attestation of the S0 grid back a further year and STRENGTHENS the carry-back; placing it at its 2018 capture date would manufacture a mid-2018 reversion to 02:00 that the 2018 (Apr) calendar, the 2019 calendar and the 2019 content-api all contradict. The 02:00-versus-04:45 ordering problem is therefore inert for Japan. RESIDUAL RISK EITHER WAY: carrying over-reports the T+1 close by up to one hour for most of 2010 on third-party press attestation (mondovisione 2010-01-08, close 01:00 effective 2010-01-11; thetradenews 2010-08-17, 01:00→02:00 on 2010-08-30), and may over-report the whole T+1 leg before 2010-01-11 — the law anticipates exactly this and says carry anyway and state it. Not carrying would report a demonstrably trading market closed for sixteen years, including the two intervals where SGX's own pages state the grid. The first error is bounded at one hour a night in one year; the second is total.
per_family.ledger_basis: **Gap: executable** — one undated changeover still falls inside an era where trades print, and the pre-2020 history is now modelled rather than sessionless. Nikkei 225 suite (NK, NS, NU, NC, NR, ND, EJP, EJRT); the modelled clock is the NK/NU index-futures grid, and NKO's continuous T phase ends at the close of the modelled `extended` window rather than at the futures close, as FCHO does on the China grid. **Five eras.** (1) From the January-2010 floor the key carries its earliest sourced grid — T 07:45–14:25, T+1 15:15–02:00, with the 14:25–14:30 closing routine — asserting **no revision row**, on the authority of SGX's own portal hours table captured 20 August 2013 and of the retired wcm/connect fragment whose contract set ("S&P CNX Nifty", "FTSE Xinhua China A50", "MSCI Asia Apex 50") dates its content to about 2012 and whose Nikkei rows are identical. That grid is also the sourced intersection with the next state, since the later grid strictly contains it in both phases. The closing routine is sourced in-era, not carried: the 2013 page's own Notes state "a 4-minute pre-closing routine before the close of the T session, followed by a 1-minute non-cancel period", its footnote states that the printed times exclude the routines, and the SGX FTSE China A50 contract specification captured the same morning prints the composed form against that page's own printed close. The opening routines stay empty — an `order_entry` gap, the lower-priority kind — because no artifact governing this era states their durations. (2) From 2017-07-10 the crate serves T 07:30–14:25 and T+1 14:55–04:45. The evidence date is SGX's derivatives Trading Hours page captured 5 July 2017, byte-identical in a second capture of 27 September 2017 and restated by the 2018 (Apr) and 2019 calendar editions, both still served live from api2.sgx.com; **a capture timestamp is used as a knowledge date and never as a cutover** — SGX changed nothing that day, and the move from the earlier grid is undated, though SGX's own product change log now brackets it in 2016 ("Equity Index & Dividend Index products T/T+1 gap increased to 15mins", issued 22 April 2016; "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours", issued 15 July 2016). The row is keyed to the following Monday because it lengthens a wrapping overnight close, and a mid-week key would report the previous evening's leg running past the close in force when it opened. Routines enter from the SGX content-api payload captured 4 February 2019 and are carried back across an interval in which no sourced bound moves. The 04:45 close is the intersection with the state that follows. (3) From 2020-01-01, the 2020 edition's grid with the 05:15 T+1 close; the T+1 open widens to 14:55 because the 2024 move is now dated and the intersection that hid it dissolves. **That 2019 change remains undated in the channels this row cites**: SGX's own voice gives only a month (Annual Report 2020) and its artifacts bracket the move between 21 June 2019 at 04:45 and its 2019-11 file directory at 05:15, so roughly seven weeks of late 2019 are under-reported by thirty minutes a night. SGX's Derivatives Products Description change log does state a day — "Effective 11 Nov: ... (T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts", inside an entry issued 7 October 2019 — and whether that channel may date a revision row is an open maintainer decision, so it is **unmodelled, not unsourceable**. (4) From 2024-11-04 the Japan T extension is dated: SGX Circular DT/AM – 50 of 2024, 9 September 2024, states "with effect from Monday, 4 November 2024, the T session trading hours for SGX Nikkei derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures will be extended by 30 minutes", lists the nine affected contracts by code, and prints Current and Revised columns that source the routines on **both** sides of its own cutover; SGX purged its own copy, so the text was read from a verbatim Fubon Futures member mirror, the same channel class as the CITIC mirror of DT/AM 15 of 2025, and SGX's own change log corroborates it ("(eff 4 Nov)", issued 4 November 2024). The circular also confirms in SGX's words that the T+1 close was already 05:15 in September 2024, so the 2019 and 2024 changes are independent rows. (5) From 2025-04-07, the current grid on DT/AM 15 of 2025, unchanged. **Partial** because two executable changeovers are undated in the channels these rows cite — the move to the 07:30 grid, undated between 2013-08-20 and 2017-07-05 though bracketed into 2016, and the 04:45→05:15 move — and because the family was not one clock before 2018: the Dividend Point contract ran 07:45–17:55 / 18:45–02:00 in 2013 and 07:30–17:55 / 18:25–04:45 in 2017, joining the Nikkei grid only in the 2018 (Apr) edition, and the Mini ran 07:45–15:25 / 16:15–02:00 until the 2017 capture, so both are over- and under-reported inside the carried eras. **Dates before the floor are the oldest state on record, not a sourced answer.**
per_family.residual_risks:
1. THIRD-PARTY ATTESTATION INSIDE THE CARRIED FLOOR INTERVAL (executable). mondovisione 2010-01-08 states a T+1 close of 01:00 effective 2010-01-11; thetradenews 2010-08-17 states 01:00 → 02:00 effective 2010-08-30. The baseline serves 02:00 from the floor, so 2010-01-01..2010-08-29 over-reports the T+1 close by up to an hour, and before 2010-01-11 the T+1 leg may not have existed in its carried form at all — the press release is headlined as an EXTENSION, so the pre-2010-01-11 close was earlier than 01:00 by an unstated amount. Carried anyway on the law's explicit instruction; the size is stated here rather than rounded down.
2. THE UNDATED S0→A CHANGEOVER (executable, under-report). The move to T open 07:30, T+1 open 14:55 and T+1 close 04:45 is undated. It is no longer unattested: SGX's own change log records an equity-index T/T+1 gap reshape issued 2016-04-22 and an NK-suite hours amendment issued 2016-07-15, neither with an effective day. If the move landed in 2016, the floor row under-reports 15 minutes of T open and up to 2h45m of T+1 close every night for about a year and a half. This is the largest remaining executable exposure in the family.
3. THE 2017-07-10 BOUNDARY RESTS ON A CAPTURE (executable, bounded). The only failure mode that would make it over-report is premature publication — SGX serving a future grid — not staleness, which runs the other way. The mitigations are the byte-identical 27 September 2017 capture, the 2018 (Apr) calendar's own "accurate as of 26 December 2017" against identical bounds, and the 2016 change-log entries that place the onset earlier still. Recorded, not eliminated.
4. THE MID-2018 SGX-VERSUS-SGX ORDERING, RESOLVED BY CONTENT DATE. The wcm fragment was captured 2018-07-11, a year after state A was live. It is resolved against the fragment on its contract set. Inert for Japan, since W's Nikkei rows equal S0's; if the resolution were wrong and SGX genuinely reverted in mid-2018, the 2017 row would over-report for that stretch.
5. ND AND NS DIVERGENCES (executable, both directions, per-member). Floor era, modelled T+1 15:15–02:00: ND actually ran 07:45–17:55 and 18:45–02:00, so it is reported open across its real 17:55–18:45 break (50 min over) and closed across 14:25–15:15 when it traded (50 min under); NS ran 07:45–15:25 / 16:15–02:00, giving the same 50/50 split. 2017 era: NS has converged, but ND ran 07:30–17:55 / 18:25–04:45, so it is reported open across its 17:55–18:25 break (30 min over) and closed across 14:30–14:55 (25 min fully closed plus the five minutes served as `extended`). Per-product scope caveat under "Product-neutral family selection", not a family error, but the module's scope note and the ledger must say it because the key advertises ND and NS without qualification.
6. FLOOR-ERA `order_entry` IS ABSENT, NOT DISPROVED. The 2013 page attests that both opening routines exist and states no duration. The lower-priority kind of gap.
7. ROUTINES ON THE 2017 ROW ARE CARRIED, NOT DIRECTLY SOURCED THERE. They come from the content-api payload of 2019-02-04, are reconfirmed by DT/AM 50's Current column in 2024, and the bounds they attach to never move across the interval — but if a routine changed inside 2017-07-10..2019-02-03 the 14:25–14:30 `extended` window, in which a trade prints, would be wrong.
8. THE 04:45→05:15 MOVE IS BRACKETED IN THE CITED CHANNELS (executable, under-report). SGX artifacts give 2019-06-21 at 04:45 and the api2 2019-11 directory at 05:15; the Mini-JGB factsheet in that directory carries an internal "Margins (As on 18-Oct-2019)" line, so its filename dates publication, not the hours. Serving 04:45 through 2019-12-31 under-reports about seven weeks by thirty minutes a night. Do NOT restate this as "every SGX channel is closed" — the product change log states a day; see open question 1.
9. DT/AM 50 IS READ FROM A MEMBER MIRROR. SGX-hosted original purged; verified against Wayback capture 20241114183232 of the Fubon Futures PDF and independently corroborated by SGX's own change log r163 and by JPX's 2023-09-20 and 2024-11-03 releases. Re-verify from an SGX-hosted copy if one becomes reachable.
10. STRUCTURAL, NOT A SCHEDULE RISK. Making the floor grid this key's baseline means the Japan key stops sharing SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_CLOSED, which must stay for the Taiwan and NTR keys. It also changes what pre-2010 instants resolve to, from sessionless to the carried grid — sanctioned explicitly by the floor convention, but an observable behaviour change that belongs in CHANGELOG.md.
per_family.open_questions:
1. ACCEPT THE PRODUCT CHANGE LOG AS A DAY-LEVEL PRIMARY? This is the one decision that would change this table. Row 89 of the Derivatives Products Description change log, inside a border-partitioned entry whose dated row is issued 2019-10-07 v6.9, reads "Effective 11 Nov:" / "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts". Accepting it inserts a dated-cutover row at Monday 2019-11-11 with T 07:30–14:25, T+1 14:55–05:15, `extended` 14:25–14:30 and `order_entry` 07:15–07:30 / 14:45–14:55, and demotes 2020-01-01 to a redundant row that should be dropped. Recorded in the store as pending with the maintainer (issue #45). The interpretive step is scoping a header row to the items below it inside one file-encoded entry; the OOXML carries zero merged cells and the border partition is the document's own structure.
2. THE 21 SEPTEMBER 2017 "CHANGE OF TRADING HOURS" NEWSLETTER IS NOT THIS FAMILY'S MOVE, and history.rs's comment naming it as the candidate should be corrected. Grid A is already live in the 2017-07-05 capture, the 2017-09-27 capture six days after the newsletter is byte-identical, and the change log's own "Change of Trading Hours" entry is issued 2017-10-05. Which notice carried the S0→A move remains unidentified; the 2016 entries suggest it is a 2016 circular.
3. CAN THE FLOOR ERA'S `order_entry` BE SOURCED? The cheapest remaining improvement. The SGX FTSE China A50 contract specification captured 20130820082329 proves that the pre-2017 portal's per-contract specification pages DID print the full session-state table. The sibling NK page from the same capture window would source both opening routines for the floor era directly. The store's `cdx_portal_equity_prefix.json` enumerates that tree; only the A50 leaf has been pulled.
4. IS THERE ANY SGX HOURS ARTIFACT BETWEEN 2013-08-20 AND 2017-07-05? The change log now proves changes happened in 2016 without stating days. Unswept channels: the archived `sgx.com/wps/wcm/connect/mp_en/...` tree for 2014–2016, SGX Monthly Market Statistics reports, and CFTC Part 48 Foreign Board of Trade filings for Singapore Exchange Derivatives Trading Ltd.
5. ARE ND'S AND NS'S CONVERGENCE DAYS DATABLE? Bracketed only — NS between 2013-08-20 and 2017-07-05, ND between 2017-09-27 and the 2018 (Apr) edition. Change-log r37, issued 2017-01-23, "Update to ND Trading Hours", is a lead and states no day. They would not change the family clock but would let a caller's catalog overlay the two members correctly.

rows.citation: earliest sourced SGX A50 grids, carried to the January-2010 floor
rows.why: ENCODED AS THIS KEY'S `select_revision` BASELINE, NOT A `revisions!` ROW; the date above is an interval label. THE T+1 OPEN IS 17:00, NOT 16:40 — this is the sharpest correction in the whole set and I side with the skeptic who quoted the law. The proposal computed each sub-interval's intersection independently and shipped the result, which made the T+1 open move INWARD, 16:40 → 17:00, on the date of a Wayback capture. A bound that widens at a knowledge boundary says "from here we have sourced this much"; a bound that NARROWS says a window that was open became closed, which is a claim about the market, not about knowledge, and it would enter HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS as an observable dated profile change that no source states. LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES: "a historical cutover exists only when a primary source states an unconditional, day-level effective date. A real change without one is documented as a known gap, never given an invented date." The crate's own worked example settles the remedy: "CME's Sunday Pre-Open ... sourced at 16:15 at the floor and 16:00 currently, so 16:15-17:00 is carried from the floor with no cutover asserted and only the 16:00-16:15 quarter-hour waits on the undated 2012 move" — the disputed remainder is withheld across the WHOLE undated span, never granted early and withdrawn at a capture. So 16:40–17:00 is withheld from the floor. Cost: twenty minutes of T+1 that both W and S0 attest, withheld for the floor interval — an under-report, the safe direction, and the price of not asserting an unsourced closure. THE OTHER BOUNDS ARE THE INTERSECTION OF W AND S0, computed bound by bound: T open max(09:00,09:00)=09:00; T close min(15:25,15:55)=15:25; T+1 close min(02:00,02:00)=02:00. ORDER_ENTRY 08:45-09:00 IS DIRECTLY SOURCED IN-ERA — the A50 contract specification captured 20130820082329 prints "Pre - Opening 8.45 am - 8.58 am / Non - Cancel 8.58 am - 9.00 am", the T open is 09:00 under W, S0 and A alike, and the identical window is printed again at 2018-10-30, 2019-01-16, 2019-02-04 and 2020-01-09. This retires the proposal's claim that 2018-10-30 is "the only in-window artifact stating ROUTINE times for any of the five families": that capture was enumerated in the store's own `cdx_portal_equity_prefix.json` and never opened. EXTENDED WITHHELD: the closing routine composes to 15:25-15:30 under W and 15:55-16:00 under S0 — disjoint — so it is genuinely disputed and is the one thing dropped. The T+1 queue window is likewise disputed (16:30-16:40 under S0, 16:50-17:00 under A) and withheld.

rows.citation: SGX portal Trading Hours grid and SGX FTSE China A50 contract specification, both captured 2013-08-20
rows.why: KIND (c). A capture used strictly as a knowledge date and NEVER as a cutover: nothing is claimed to have changed on 2013-08-20; what changes is that from that day SGX is observed publishing S0, which excludes W from later intervals. The load-bearing argument is directional — a served page can be stale but never early, so a capture is a sound upper bound on when the state it shows began, and using it can only under-date the onset. ONLY THE T CLOSE MOVES, AND IT WIDENS, 15:25 → 15:55, so no closure is dated and the row is admissible. The T+1 open stays 17:00 for the reason given in the baseline row; the T+1 close stays 02:00 as min(02:00, 04:45). EXTENDED 15:55-16:00: under S0 this is the closing auction, printed verbatim by the same morning's specification page ("Pre - Closing 3.55 pm - 3.59 pm / Non - Cancel 3.59 pm - 4.00 pm"); under A the same span is inside the continuous 09:00–16:30 T session. So the window is executable under EVERY state admissible in this interval, and serving it as `extended` claims tradeability under both while under-claiming only the phase KIND under A. That is exactly "serve the window that holds under *every* sourced state and withhold only the disputed remainder", and withholding it instead would blank a printable window for four years. NOT ROUNDED TO A MONDAY: this row changes only a daytime close, and its wrapping T+1 rule is identical on both sides, so no running session is split.

rows.citation: SGX derivatives Trading Hours page, captures 2017-07-05 and 2017-09-27; routines from the SGX A50 contract specification, capture 2018-10-30
rows.why: KIND (c), keyed to the earliest artifact attesting state A: "CN | FTSE China A50 Index Futures | 9:00 am to 4:30 pm | 5.00 pm to 4.45 am", byte-identical on the English site twelve weeks later. Again a capture as a knowledge date, never a cutover. The 2016 change-log entries ("Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours", issued 2016-07-15, naming CN explicitly) place the onset earlier still, which makes this row conservative rather than early. KEYED TO MONDAY 2017-07-10 because it lengthens the wrapping overnight close from 02:00 to 04:45 and a mid-week key would report the Tuesday-night leg open to 04:45 on that morning — a false open of 2h45m that the module's "DIRECTION OF THE ERROR" note promises these rows can no longer produce. INTERSECTION OVER {A, B, B', C}: A, B and B' are identical for China (the A→B' moves are the NTR suite's arrival and the SiMSCI pair, neither touching CN), and C differs only in the universal T+1 close, so T 09:00–16:30, T+1 open 17:00, T+1 close min(04:45,05:15)=04:45. ROUTINES ENTER HERE, NOT AT A SEPARATE 2018-10-30 ROW — I collapse the proposal's fourth row. Its stated basis, "the first source that lists the modelled product WITH its routine times", is refuted by the 2013 specification page. The values come from the 2018-10-30 capture, verbatim "Pre - Opening: 8.45 am - 8.58 am / Non - Cancel: 8.58 am - 9.00 am / Opening: 9.00 am - 4.30 pm / Pre - Closing: 4.30 pm - 4.34 pm / Non - Cancel: 4.34 pm - 4.35 pm", T+1 "Pre - Opening: 4.50 pm - 4.58 pm / Non - Cancel: 4.58 pm - 5.00 pm", repeated unchanged at 2019-01-16, 2019-02-04 and 2020-01-09 and matching DT/AM 15 of 2025's Current column at the far end. They attach to a T close unanimous across the whole interval and 08:45–09:00 is additionally sourced at the interval's far side in 2013, so carrying them to the era's start is the same move the baseline row makes, and leaving sixteen months of empty routine columns would omit an executable window for no evidentiary gain.

rows.why: UNCHANGED — SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_CHINA_BASELINE exactly as it ships, and the family's only dated cutover. DT/AM 15 of 2025, 24 February 2025, "with effect from Monday, [7] April 2025", Appendix A giving China's revised Pre-Opening/Non-Cancel/Opening as 16:40 / 16:43 / 16:45. Corroborated in a second SGX channel by change-log r170, issued 2025-03-19, "(eff 7 Apr)". A Monday, so the boundary splits no running session. This row is what makes the routine chain self-consistent end to end: the circular's Current column is the 16:50/16:53/17:00 window the 2013, 2018, 2019 and 2020 SGX artifacts state, so the order-entry phase is now continuously sourced from the floor to the present with one dated move in the middle.

per_family.floor_decision: (iii) — NEITHER a single carried state NOR sessionless. The floor..2017-07-10 span splits at the one dated artifact inside it into two intervals, and one bound is held flat across both to keep the split honest. [2010-01-01, 2013-08-20) serves T 09:00–15:25 / T+1 17:00–02:00; [2013-08-20, 2017-07-10) serves T 09:00–15:55 / T+1 17:00–02:00. WHY NOT SESSIONLESS: "'Unsourced' means 'not worked up', never 'no source exists' ... This repository shipped 'no edition of the calendar survives before it' for SGX while the operator's own pre-2020 hours pages sat in the archive stating a materially different grid. A sessionless era is a safe answer either way, but the stated reason has to be true." Three SGX-authored artifacts state CN's grid below 2017. WHY NOT ONE CARRIED WINDOW: that would silently discard W, an SGX-authored primary that names CN with a grid, and would over-report the pre-2013 T session by thirty minutes. "Prefer the sourced intersection to omission" applies per interval, and the states admissible in [floor, 2013-08-20) are W and S0, not A — S0 is directly observed on 2013-08-20, which excludes A from before it, and no evidence supports an A→S0→A reversion. WHY THE T+1 OPEN IS STILL HELD FLAT AT 17:00: because the two intersections would otherwise disagree in the narrowing direction, and a knowledge boundary may not narrow. That is the CME rule applied to a three-state sequence, and it is the correction the skeptic won on the law. W TREATED BY CONTENT DATE: its contract set ("S&P CNX Nifty", "FTSE Xinhua China A50", "MSCI Asia Apex 50", "MSCI Hong Kong+") places it around 2012, and LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES means it can key no row of its own — its state may only enter an intersection. The consequence of the content-date reading is that W lands entirely inside the carried floor interval, which is the only place it can bite; read at its capture date it would force a 2018 regression that the 2018 (Apr) calendar, the 2018-10-30 specification page and the 2019 artifacts all contradict. RESIDUAL RISK EITHER WAY: carrying asserts a 02:00 T+1 close from 2010-01-01 while third-party press attests 01:00 until 2010-08-30 — the law says carry anyway and state it; leaving the interval sessionless would report a demonstrably trading contract closed for seven years, in the direction the crate calls the worse error.
per_family.ledger_basis: **Gap: executable** — the uncertainty touches windows where trades print, so this row's history is served conservatively and the basis says how. FTSE China A50 (CN); the H50 futures and options (FCH, FCHO) appear in no pre-2020 SGX artifact and join the family's calendar listing at the 2021 edition, after the family clock began, so they move no boundary. Current T 09:00–16:30 and T+1 16:45 sessions sourced. Five eras, of which only the last is a dated cutover. **The pre-2020 era is no longer sessionless.** The January-2010 baseline carries the intersection of the two oldest sourced SGX grids for CN — the orphaned `wps/wcm/connect` Trading Hours fragment, captured 11 July 2018 but dated to about 2012 by its contract set ("FTSE Xinhua China A50" 9.00 am–3.25 pm / 4.10 pm–2.00 am), and the portal Trading Hours grid captured 20 August 2013 ("SGX FTSE China A50 Index Futures" 9.00am–3.55pm / 4.40pm–2.00am) — serving T 09:00–15:25 and T+1 17:00–02:00 and asserting **no revision row**. The T+1 open is held at 17:00 from the floor rather than surrendered later: the 16:40–17:00 remainder is disputed by an undated changeover and is withheld across the whole span, exactly as CME's Sunday Pre-Open withholds 16:00–16:15, because a knowledge boundary may widen what the crate serves and may never narrow it. The orphan is placed before the 2013 grid on its contract set; the 2013 document's own per-holiday tables print the A50 at 3.25pm/4.10pm while its normal-week table prints 3.55pm/4.40pm, which corroborates the order but no more, since the A50 is the only contract in those tables that departs from its normal-week row. From 2013-08-20 the T session widens to 15:55 on the grid that capture attests, with the 15:55–16:00 closing auction that the **SGX FTSE China A50 contract specification captured the same morning** prints verbatim; from 2017-07-10, on the two byte-identical portal captures of 5 July and 27 September 2017, it is T 09:00–16:30 with T+1 17:00–04:45, which under-reports roughly November–December 2019 by thirty minutes rather than over-reporting it. Both pre-2020 boundaries are **knowledge dates keyed to the artifact that first attests the state, never cutovers, and neither narrows a window**: a served page can be stale but never early — the 2018 orphan is the proof, and so is SGX's own commodities hours page, which was still printing a 2.00 am T+1 close for iron ore fifty minutes after the 27 September 2017 derivatives capture printed 4.45am for the same contract — so a capture is a sound upper bound on a state's onset. The 2017 row is keyed to the following Monday because it lengthens a wrapping overnight close and a mid-week key would report the previous evening's leg running past the close in force when it opened. Routines are sourced continuously from the floor: the 2013 specification page states "Pre - Opening 8.45 am - 8.58 am / Non - Cancel 8.58 am - 9.00 am ... Pre - Closing 3.55 pm - 3.59 pm / Non - Cancel 3.59 pm - 4.00 pm" and the T+1 pair 4.30/4.38/4.40 pm, the 2018-10-30 specification page states the same shape against the 4.30 pm grid, and the content-api repeats it unchanged in 2019 and 2020; the 2020-01-01 row therefore carries them too. SGX's own product change log names two undated amendments inside the unmodelled window — "Equity Index & Dividend Index products T/T+1 gap increased to 15mins" issued 22 April 2016 and "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours" issued 15 July 2016 — so the transition is **unmodelled, not unsourceable**, and 2016 is not the hole it was recorded as. SGX Circular DT/AM – 50 of 2024 does **not** split this family's era: it enumerates nine Japan contracts and names no A50 contract. Partial because the two pre-2020 transition days are unmodelled and because third-party press (mondovisione, 8 January 2010; The Trade, 17 August 2010) attests a T+1 close of 01:00 until 30 August 2010, inside the carried interval; the crate carries the 02:00 state anyway and records the risk here.
per_family.residual_risks:
1. THIRD-PARTY ATTESTATION INSIDE THE CARRIED INTERVAL (executable, over-report). 01:00 effective 2010-01-11, 01:00 → 02:00 on 2010-08-30. The floor row serves 02:00 from 2010-01-01, so it over-reports the T+1 close by up to an hour through most of 2010 and may over-report the whole leg before 2010-01-11. Carried on the law's explicit instruction.
2. UNOBSERVED INTERMEDIATE STATES (executable). The 2014–2016 hours pages are unrecovered. Every observed A50 move is a widening of the T close (15:25 → 15:55 → 16:30) and a lengthening of the T+1 close, so a monotone intermediate remains a superset of the served window — but that is an inference, not a source, and SGX's change log now confirms a CN hours amendment was issued 2016-07-15 without stating a day.
3. THE T+1 OPEN IS WITHHELD FROM 16:40 TO 17:00 IN THE FLOOR INTERVAL (executable, under-report). Twenty minutes a night that both W and S0 attest, for the whole floor interval, deliberately withheld so that no unsourced closure is dated. This is the price of the correction and it must be stated, not hidden.
4. W IS UNDATED. Its placement before S0 rests on its contract set; the holiday-table corroboration is weaker than the proposal claimed, since the A50 is the only contract in those tables that departs from its normal-week row and three of the seven dates postdate the capture. If the ordering is wrong, both the floor and 2013 rows mis-serve. Because W enters only through intersections, and an intersection can only narrow, the error would be one-directional and conservative.
5. STALENESS DIRECTION ON THE CAPTURE-KEYED ROWS. SGX demonstrably served mutually contradictory hours pages at the same time — the commodities tree at 2017-06-06 and 2017-09-27 still printed the 02:00 regime for contracts the derivatives tree gave at 04:45. Staleness makes content older than reality, so it would mean state A began earlier and the rows under-claim; the only failure that would over-report is premature publication, which the 2016 change-log entries now argue against. The 2017 commodities-versus-derivatives conflict is recorded here as AGENTS.md requires for a source conflict, though it touches no equity-index contract (the commodities page carries none — I grepped it).
6. `extended` IS WITHHELD IN THE FLOOR ERA. The closing routine composes to 15:25-15:30 under W and 15:55-16:00 under S0, disjoint, so it is genuinely disputed and dropped. An executable under-report of five minutes a day for the floor interval.
7. TRANSCRIPTION CONFLICT, RESOLVED. `2026-09-06-grids-intermediate-2019-state.json` reports the 2018-07-11 page's A50 as "7.45 am - 3.25 pm / 4.15 pm"; that is the Mini Nikkei 225 row. I re-extracted the raw HTML: the A50 row is "9.00 am - 3.25 pm | 4.10 pm - 2.00 am (following day)". The intersection is unaffected either way.
8. NO 2024 CHINA CIRCULAR IS IN EVIDENCE, and none is needed — DT/AM 50 names no A50 contract and the 2024 and 2025-01 calendars show no China change.
9. STRUCTURAL. Giving this key its own baseline changes what pre-2010 instants resolve to, from sessionless to the carried grid; sanctioned by the floor convention but an observable behaviour change for CHANGELOG.md. SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_CLOSED must survive for the Taiwan and NTR keys.
10. STORE DEFECT THAT WILL MISLEAD THE NEXT READER. `2026-09-06-grids-portal-hours-page.json` dead-end 3 states that the 2013-08-20 capture "does not carry the standard grid — at that date the page held a holiday trading schedule". That is false: I extracted the page and the full "Trading Hours* for SGX Derivatives Market" table sits below the holiday tables, and every S0 value in the brief comes from it. `2026-09-06-grids-contract-sets-and-boundaries.json` records it correctly. Reconcile before this evidence is used again.
per_family.open_questions:
1. WHAT DATED THE A50'S TWO PRE-2017 EXTENSIONS? The moves 15:25 → 15:55 / 16:10 → 16:40 and 15:55 → 16:30 / 16:40 → 17:00 are A50-specific in the first case and shared in the second. The Titan "Change of Trading Hours" newsletter of 21 Sep 2017 is ruled OUT: the 2017-07-05 and 2017-09-27 captures straddle it and diff clean, and SGX's own change log dates its "Change of Trading Hours" entry to 2017-10-05. Change-log r27, issued 2016-07-15, "Amendments to NK suite, CH, CHO and CN trading hours", is the strongest lead and states no day.
2. IS THERE A PRE-2013 SGX A50 SPECIFICATION PAGE? The 2013-08-20 capture proves the specification tree carried full session tables. An earlier capture of the same leaf would source the W-era routines directly and could confirm or refute W's ordering.
3. THE SAME UNOPENED-CAPTURE FAILURE PROBABLY SITS UNDER THE JAPAN AND SINGAPORE KEYS. `cdx_portal_equity_prefix.json` enumerates sibling specification leaves under `.../equity/nikkei_225_futures_options/` and `.../equity/sgx_simsci/`; only 2021 captures of those were retrieved. Re-walking that enumeration is the cheapest remaining improvement to two families' floor eras and must be opened as an issue under LAW-FOLLOW-UPS-ARE-ISSUES.
4. SHOULD DT/AM 15 OF 2025's APPENDIX A "Current" COLUMN BE QUOTED VERBATIM into the module as the second witness for the 16:50–17:00 queue? history.rs quotes only the revised column. Reading it directly would remove the last inference in the routine chain.
5. DO FCH / FCHO SHARE THE CN GRID, and does FCHO's later T close warrant its own key rather than the shared China key? Out of scope for this pass; the module's own comment already flags the divergence.
6. THE 2013-08-20 CAPTURE ALSO HOLDS SGX'S FULL PER-DATE HOLIDAY SCHEDULE FOR 2013. Caller-owned under LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE and out of this crate's scope, but it is the richest surviving SGX date-exception record for the period and should be pointed at `docs/schedules/date-exceptions.md`.

per_family.family: sgx_equity_index_singapore — SiMSCI + Straits Times Index (SGP, SGPO/CSGP, ST). Modelled on the SGP futures grid; the options row's five extra continuous minutes coincide with the futures' closing routine in every sourced era, so one window serves both.
per_family.members: SGP — "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures" in the 2013-08-20 portal capture (combined row with ST), in both 2017 portal captures (code SGP, "8.30am to 5.10 pm | 5.40 pm to 4.45 am") and again in the 2020 and 2021 editions; "SGX MSCI Singapore Free Index Futures" in the 2018 (Apr) calendar line 868, the 2019 calendar line 898 and content-api 20190204200905 / 20190611051800 / 20200109051211. One code, one product; "Free" is added around 2018 and dropped again by 2020. SGPO — "MSCI Singapore Index Options" (2013 portal, printed without the SGX prefix, 8.30am–5.15pm), "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Options" (2017 portal, 5.15 pm), "SGX MSCI Singapore Free Index Options" (2018/2019 calendars, content-api). Continuous. ST — "SGX Straits Times Index Futures" from 2013-08-20 onward; the 2013 portal prints SGP and ST in one combined hours row and every later artifact gives ST the SGP grid (2018 line 891, 2019 line 853). CONSEQUENCE: this family has NO product-driven knowledge boundary above the floor — the three codes are listed in the earliest hours artifact on record — which is precisely what makes the carry-back available here and unavailable to FTSE Taiwan. THE MSCI/FTSE QUESTION, DECIDED: the family never became FTSE. The 2020-08-20 FTSE Russell release foreshadows only FTSE EPRA Nareit Asia ex-Japan and Asia ex-Japan / EM Asia NTR and Price Return futures; the 2020-07-01 release names only FTSE Taiwan. The decisive negative is the 2021 calendar — the first edition after the MSCI Taiwan deletion — which still lists SGP as "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures" plus SGPO and NSP under MSCI branding, with no FTSE Singapore contract anywhere in it. So "MSCI S'pore" / "MSCI Singapore Free" / "MSCI Singapore" are three names for SGP, and this is a continuous rename, not a succession.

They belong to `sgx_equity_index_ntr_usd`, and NSG's first gridded listing — the 2018 (Apr) calendar, line 870 — sets that key's boundary, not this one's. rows.citation: earliest sourced SGX SiMSCI/STI grid, carried to the January-2010 floor
rows.why: ENCODED AS THE KEY'S `select_revision` BASELINE, NOT A `revisions!` ROW — I accept the skeptic's correction: the proposal printed this as `effective 2010-01-01 / intersection-start` while its own prose said it asserts no revision row, and the printed form would have fabricated a cutover at the audit floor and added the lower bound the floor convention forbids ("Do not add a lower bound to the timelines"). The date above is an interval label only. LAW quoted: "Carry the earliest sourced state back to the audit floor ... This asserts *no* revision row, so it does not fabricate a date - it declines to invent one." ARTIFACTS: the 2013-08-20 portal capture, main table, verbatim "SGX MSCI Singapore Index Futures / SGX Straits Times Index Futures | 8.30am to 5.10pm | 6.15pm to 2.00am", with the options row at 5.15pm; corroborated for SiMSCI and the options by the wcm fragment whose content dates to about 2012.
